text.p: Precision engineering company CAM International Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it was rationalising its operations in the Philippines, Singapore, Malaysia and China as part of expansion plans.
The company said in a statement its operations in Johor Baru, Malaysia would be cut back, leaving only a small operation to take care of existing customers.
Equipment and business would be transferred to the Philippines and China from Johor Baru "to cater to the growing number of customers there", it said.
It said the initial investment for the Philippines and China were Singapore $3 million and S$2 million respectively for the financial year to September 30, 1996.

In a separate statement, CAM said it would sell 52.5 percent of its Malaysian unit CAM Precision Components (Penang) Sdn Bhd to Malaysian investor Datuk Hamzah, Essex Investment (Singapore) Pte and Corex Technology (S) Pte Ltd for S$9.55 million.
It said the sale of CPP, which accounted for about 47 percent of group profits in its 1995 financial year, would decrease the group's profits by approximately 25 percent.
However, it said higher earnings by the Malaysian unit due to the "strategic alliance" with the new majority owners should compensate for the decrease in its stake in the unit.
